claims.claim: The 2018 Buolamwini/Gebru study found commercial facial-analysis error rates of at most 0.8% for light-skinned men but over 20-34% for darker-skinned women.
claims.episode_span: A 2018 study by Joy Buolamwini and Timnit Gebru at MIT documented large accuracy gaps across skin tones and genders in several commercial systems then in use.
claims.source_title: Study finds gender and skin-type bias in commercial artificial-intelligence systems | MIT News
claims.supporting_quote: In the researchers’ experiments, the three programs’ error rates in determining the gender of light-skinned men were never worse than 0.8 percent. For darker-skinned women, however, the error rates ballooned — to more than 20 percent in one case and more than 34 percent in the other two.

claims.claim: Robert Williams was wrongfully arrested outside his home by Detroit police based on a false facial-recognition match to a store theft he did not commit.
claims.episode_span: a man named Robert Williams was arrested in his Detroit driveway after a facial-recognition match linked him to a department-store theft he had not committed
claims.source_title: Williams v. City of Detroit | American Civil Liberties Union
claims.supporting_quote: In January 2020, Detroit police wrongfully arrested our client Robert Williams outside his home , in front of his two young daughters and wife and in plain view of his neighbors, and subjected him to thirty hours of detention in an overcrowded, dirty cell.

claims.claim: Clearview AI built a facial-search database of billions of images scraped from the internet, sold primarily to law enforcement.
claims.episode_span: Clearview AI scraped billions of web photos to sell facial-search services to law enforcement
claims.supporting_quote: The company's algorithm matches faces to a database of more than 20 billion images collected from the Internet, including social media applications.

claims.claim: In May 2019 San Francisco became the first major US city to ban government use of facial recognition.
claims.episode_span: San Francisco and several other cities banned municipal use of facial recognition
claims.supporting_quote: In May 2019, San Francisco, California became the first major United States city to ban the use of facial recognition software for police and other local government agencies' usage.

claims.claim: Apple introduced Face ID with the iPhone X in 2017.
claims.episode_span: Apple’s 2017 introduction of Face ID on the iPhone X was presented as a convenience feature that also raised the bar for device security.
claims.supporting_quote: Apple announced Face ID alongside the iPhone X on September 12, 2017, at the Steve Jobs Theater
